scenes.tts: Put an electrode inside a resting frog muscle fibre, at the endplate, where the nerve ends. Stimulate nothing. Small depolarizations still arrive at random times. Each is about the same size, and each is far too small to fire the fibre. What are they?
scenes.visual: Nerve terminal over a muscle fibre with an electrode inside; the nerve is not stimulated; a voltage sketch fills with small equal blips at random times, far below a dashed line that fires the fibre; a question mark ends the scene.
scenes.narration: Put an electrode inside a resting frog muscle fibre, at the endplate, where the nerve ends. Stimulate nothing. Small depolarizations still arrive at random times. Each is about the same size, and each is far too small to fire the fibre. What are they?

scenes.tts: These are miniature endplate potentials. Fatt and Katz attributed them to spontaneous release of acetylcholine from the nerve terminal. Del Castillo and Katz asked whether a nerve impulse evokes the same units. They bathed the frog junction in less calcium and more magnesium, which cut release to a trickle. Now an impulse often produced nothing at all, a failure.
scenes.visual: A packet of acetylcholine leaves the terminal as a blip appears; an impulse runs down the axon; calcium and magnesium chips appear and packets thin to one; a grid of twelve trials shows empty boxes turning red as failures.

scenes.tts: When a response did come, its size was not random. The amplitudes clustered at the size of one miniature, at twice that, and at three times that. So the evoked response came in packets. Each packet is a quantum, a packet of many molecules, later identified with the contents of one vesicle. It is not one molecule of acetylcholine.
scenes.visual: The twelve trials drop as dots into columns at zero, one, two and three miniatures; then a packet of many dots grows on the left, is wrapped by one vesicle outline, and a single dot is marked as not the quantum.

scenes.tts: The mean quantal content is the average number of quanta one impulse releases. Take a made-up frog junction in low calcium and high magnesium. The mean miniature and the mean response, failures included, are both zero point four zero millivolts. So the ratio is one quantum per stimulus. Failures give a second estimate, since seventy four of two hundred stimuli gave no response.
scenes.caption: The mean quantal content is the average number of quanta one impulse releases. Take a made-up frog junction in low calcium and high magnesium. The mean miniature and the mean response, failures included, are both 0.40 mV. So the ratio is one quantum per stimulus. Failures give a second estimate, since 74 of 200 stimuli gave no response.
scenes.visual: Two bars of equal height give 0.40 over 0.40 equals 1.00 on the left; on the right a grid of 200 squares fills 74 red and gives 74 over 200 equals 0.37.

scenes.tts: Under a Poisson model, minus the natural log of zero point three seven is zero point nine nine. The two estimates agree. Now suppose sixty quanta of zero point four zero millivolts each in normal calcium. If they add linearly, that is twenty four millivolts against a threshold of twelve. Toy values; real frog values differ. The safety factor, the ratio of the two, is two.

If they add linearly, that is 24 mV against a threshold of 12. Toy values; real frog values differ. The safety factor, the ratio of the two, is 2.
scenes.visual: The failure column gains minus the natural log of 0.37 equals 0.99 and the two estimates are joined as agreeing; the scene clears and a bar of sixty quanta rises to 24 mV past a dashed line at 12 mV; the safety factor 2.0 is marked.

scenes.tts: In myasthenia gravis, fewer receptors mean a smaller quantal size, and sixty of them still fire the fibre. But suppose release runs down by twenty five percent, to forty five quanta. The response is then ten point eight millivolts, and the fibre fails. Miniature size also depends on vesicle filling, so confirm with a receptor count. So smaller miniatures point to receptors or filling, and fewer packets point before the synapse.
